name.title: Device name
name.what: A label for this saved source device, not its network address.
name.how: Use a meaningful nonempty name; saving does not start acquisition.

protocol.title: Communication protocol
protocol.what: Selects how the gateway communicates with the device.
protocol.how: Match the device manual. Only enabled protocols are available; MQTT is not enabled by this form.
protocol.example: Modbus TCP for a device configured for Modbus TCP.

host.title: Device host
host.what: The device hostname or IP reachable from the gateway.
host.how: Use the device network settings, not the browser computer address. A saved draft is not a successful probe.
host.example: 192.0.2.10 is an example, not a reachable default.

port.title: Device port
port.what: The network service port used by the selected protocol.
port.how: Match the configured PLC service. Protocol defaults differ; validation still applies.
port.example: Modbus TCP commonly uses 502; FATEK TCP default 500 and MC3E default 5000 are not universal settings.

modbusSlave.title: Modbus slave ID
modbusSlave.how: TCP/RTU schema accepts integers 1–247. Match the addressed slave.
modbusSlave.example: 1 when the device is configured as slave 1.

udpSlave.title: Modbus UDP slave ID
udpSlave.how: Match the UDP connector and device configuration; do not assume another transport’s limits.
udpSlave.example: The connector default is 1; confirm the device setting.

fatekStation.title: FATEK station
fatekStation.how: The FATEK schema accepts 0–255. Match the PLC station in the selected TCP or serial mode.

mcStation.title: MC3E station
mcStation.how: Use the station in the PLC routing configuration, not a Modbus slave ID.

timeoutModbus.title: Response timeout (seconds)
timeoutModbus.how: TCP/RTU schema accepts 1–60 seconds. This is a response deadline, not the sampling or SQL interval.

timeoutOther.title: Response timeout (seconds)
timeoutOther.how: Use the selected connector’s timeout validation. This is not the sampling or SQL interval.
timeoutOther.example: The displayed connector default is 5 seconds.

fatekMode.title: FATEK connection mode
fatekMode.how: Choose TCP or serial to match the PLC. The two modes have different connection fields.
fatekMode.example: Serial exposes the gateway host serial port and line settings.

serialPort.title: Gateway serial port
serialPort.how: Use a serial device on the gateway host, not the browser computer.
serialPort.example: /dev/ttyUSB0 or COM1, only if that port exists on the gateway.

baudModbus.title: Modbus RTU baud rate
baudModbus.how: Choose 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600 or 115200 to match the device. The dropdown is the canonical RTU enum.
baudModbus.example: 9600 bits per second when both ends use 9600.

baudFatek.title: FATEK serial baud rate
baudFatek.how: Match the PLC serial configuration. FATEK does not borrow the Modbus RTU dropdown restriction.

parity.title: Serial parity
parity.how: Choose none, even or odd to match both ends. FATEK and RTU defaults differ.
parity.example: FATEK defaults to even; Modbus RTU defaults to none.

dataBits.title: Serial data bits
dataBits.how: The current form offers 7 or 8 bits; match the device configuration.

stopBits.title: Serial stop bits
stopBits.how: Choose 1 or 2 stop bits to match the device.

networkNo.title: MC network number
networkNo.how: Use the network number from the PLC route; change only when routing requires it.

pcNo.title: MC PC number
pcNo.how: Use the destination PC number from the PLC route, not the workstation name.

ioNo.title: MC I/O number
ioNo.how: Use the routed module I/O number. The existing decoder also recognizes the module_io_no alias.

dataFormat.title: Connection byte/word order
dataFormat.what: The default decoding order used for applicable source values.
dataFormat.how: Match the PLC register representation. ABCD/BADC/CDAB/DCBA change decoding, not this recording’s calculation.
dataFormat.example: Use the device manual to identify ABCD versus CDAB.

mqttBroker.title: Legacy MQTT broker
mqttBroker.what: The broker address retained by the existing MQTT configuration view.
mqttBroker.how: MQTT is not enabled for new source creation here. This explanation does not add protocol support.

mqttUsername.title: Legacy MQTT username
mqttUsername.what: The optional user name for the existing broker configuration.
mqttUsername.how: Use the broker account identifier. Help never displays stored credentials.

mqttClientId.title: Legacy MQTT client ID
mqttClientId.what: The identifier retained for the existing MQTT client.
mqttClientId.how: Use the identifier required by the existing broker setup; this does not enable MQTT acquisition.

name.title: Point-name prefix
name.what: Generates initial point names and identifies this source range. Each point’s display name can be changed later.
name.how: Enter a recognizable prefix; it is normalized before saving. This is not a database column name.
name.example: Prefix TEMP and address D0 produce TEMP_D0.

address.title: Starting address
address.what: The first PLC address in this source range.
address.how: Use the selected protocol’s address syntax and register area. Width is determined by the data type.
address.example: Modbus 40001 and MC D0 are different protocol examples, not interchangeable.

count.title: Number of points
count.what: How many values to create, not the number of network requests.
count.how: Use a positive integer within the protocol/address geometry. There is no universal 64-point limit.
count.example: Three float32 points occupy six 16-bit registers.

dataType.title: Source data type
dataType.what: How the register bytes are decoded into each source value.
dataType.how: Choose a type supported by the selected protocol and address. A numeric-looking value does not prove its type.
dataType.example: float32 consumes two 16-bit registers; int16 consumes one.

scale.title: Source multiplier
scale.what: Multiplies the decoded value before the offset is added.
scale.how: Use a finite number from the device specification; this changes the shared source, not only one recording.
scale.example: Raw 123 with multiplier 0.1 and offset 0 represents 12.3.

offset.title: Source offset
offset.what: Adds a constant after source scaling.
offset.how: Use a finite number in the resulting engineering unit. Keep critical source changes explicit.

dataFormat.title: Range byte/word order
dataFormat.what: Selects decoding order for this shared acquisition range.
dataFormat.how: Use the device register layout. Default inherits existing decoding rules; it is not a calculation mode.
dataFormat.example: ABCD and CDAB represent different arrangements of the same four bytes.

unit.title: Point unit label
unit.what: The engineering unit recorded on generated point mappings.
unit.how: A unit label alone does not rescale values or establish counter semantics.
unit.example: V for volts after the correct multiplier is configured.

order.title: Per-point decoding order
order.what: Word order controls how bytes and words form a multiword value; this setting belongs to the shared source point.
order.how: For supported multiword points, choose the source default or an override and save it. The change affects recordings using this point; saving does not mean it has been applied to active collection.
order.example: An int16 uses one 16-bit word and keeps native decoding; a 32-bit point can specify CDAB.

name.title: Recording name
name.what: A human-readable name for this recording, not a table identity.
name.how: Enter a nonempty name; renaming does not transfer schema ownership.

strategy.title: Managed or existing table
strategy.what: Chooses the existing managed-table or custom-table contract.
strategy.how: Managed ownership and schema checks still apply. Selecting a strategy does not create or modify a table.
strategy.example: Reuse only a compatible configured destination, never another wide-table owner.

table.title: Destination table
table.what: The canonical table receiving this recording.
table.how: Managed long-table names come from the backend; locked names are not editable aliases. Custom tables require current metadata.
table.example: A configured table selection fills intent only, not schema consent.

schema.title: Database schema
schema.what: The destination namespace, where supported by the database.
schema.how: Use the existing connector and ownership rules. The same table name in another schema is a different destination.
schema.example: public is a PostgreSQL schema example, not a universal default.

method.title: Recording method
method.what: Latest stores the last eligible reading in the window; mean is the arithmetic mean of eligible readings; delta records a confirmed counter's change in the window.
method.how: Each point has its own UTC-aligned windows. Wide tables leave not-due points NULL (not_due); long tables write due points only. No carry-forward and no zero fill.
method.example: One recording can store temperature as latest every 15 s and energy as delta every 10 min.

layout.title: Recording layout
layout.what: Wide layouts place members in one row; long layouts store a row per member result.
layout.how: Use only enabled layouts. Saved ownership/layout cannot be silently converted by this choice.
layout.example: Independent members can have different UTC-aligned due windows in a mixed record.

method.title: Result to record
method.what: Latest stores the last reading; mean averages measurements; delta records a confirmed counter interval change.
method.how: A disabled option means this source cannot use it yet: mean needs “Confirm measurement use” on the row, delta needs a confirmed counter definition. Counter raw/state are not averaged automatically; the first counter baseline is not zero.
method.example: The same source can use latest in one record and mean in another.

cadence.title: Member interval
cadence.what: The UTC-epoch-aligned window for this member, separate from acquisition polling.
cadence.how: Enter an integer within the current backend bounds shown inline. Not yet due is not a failed sample.
cadence.example: A 5-second member and a 60-second member become due independently.

cadenceUnit.title: Interval unit
cadenceUnit.what: The unit of this member’s recording window.
cadenceUnit.how: Choose a unit offered by the current capability: seconds or minutes. This is not a rate multiplier.

include.title: Include this source
include.what: Controls whether this saved source belongs to the recording draft.
include.how: Removing membership does not delete the shared source or its history.
include.example: Exclude an unused point without changing its PLC definition.

required.title: Required point
required.what: When enabled, this point is a required source for this recording. It does not change the device or other recordings.
required.how: When a due point has no valid data, the recording format and missing-data policy may skip the output. Optional points still follow that policy and do not guarantee a write. Save the recording settings to apply a change.
required.example: If required temperature data is missing, a skip policy may omit the record. When partial writes are supported, an optional missing value can retain NULL and a reason, rather than an invented zero.

targetColumn.title: Destination column
targetColumn.what: Maps this member to a compatible SQL column.
targetColumn.how: Select from current metadata or an explicit schema proposal. A proposed column does not already exist.
targetColumn.example: temperature for a compatible numeric source.

entityKey.title: Member entity key
entityKey.what: The per-member identity written to the configured entity column.
entityKey.how: Use a stable distinguishable value when the selected layout exposes this field.
entityKey.example: line-a-meter rather than a secret or changing display value.

gaugeConfirm.title: Confirm measurement meaning
gaugeConfirm.what: Confirms that this numeric source is a measurement for this recording’s mean calculation.
gaugeConfirm.how: This record-only confirmation is bound to the source context; it does not edit the shared definition or approve a counter.
gaugeConfirm.example: Voltage is a measurement only when its real source meaning is verified.

interval.title: Row interval (seconds)
interval.what: The recording window for this non-profile row.
interval.how: Use a positive interval accepted by the existing validator. Polling cadence is configured separately.
interval.example: 15 seconds is a window, not 15 PLC reads.

lateness.title: Allowed lateness (seconds)
lateness.what: How long a recording window can accept late source observations before finalization.
lateness.how: Use a nonnegative value accepted by the current policy. Closed snapshots are not silently rewritten.
lateness.example: 0 adds no lateness allowance; it does not mean missing values become 0.

incomplete.title: Incomplete row policy
incomplete.what: What to do when a row lacks required source data.
incomplete.how: Choose the offered skip-row or partial policy. Required members and nullable schema still constrain the result.
incomplete.example: Partial data keeps unavailable values distinguishable from true zero.

dedupe.title: Delivery deduplication
dedupe.what: The existing receipt capability used to avoid duplicating accepted delivery.
dedupe.how: Managed tables use receipt ownership; do not infer successful SQL from this selection.
dedupe.example: Receipt selection does not replace a fresh schema check.

entityColumn.title: Entity key column
entityColumn.what: The SQL column storing the member’s entity key where configured.
entityColumn.how: Use a compatible column and current schema validation; a name alone does not create it.
entityColumn.example: entity_id, only when the target schema supports it.

provenanceColumn.title: Provenance column
provenanceColumn.what: The SQL column retaining recording provenance where configured.
provenanceColumn.how: Use the existing schema contract; this is not a free-form secret or connection field.
provenanceColumn.example: source_info as an explicitly compatible column.

pool.title: Existing database connection
pool.what: Selects a saved connector identity and revision.
pool.how: Only enabled supported connectors can be selected. Credentials are not copied into help.
pool.example: Choose the saved production SQLite connector, then review its destination.

kind.title: Database kind
kind.what: Chooses the existing database connector capability.
kind.how: Only currently enabled kinds can be used. A listed or disabled kind is not a promise of runtime support.
kind.example: SQLite is file based; PostgreSQL uses a server connection.

name.title: Connection name
name.what: A display name for the database connection.
name.how: Use a meaningful label; this is not the database filename or credential.

host.title: Database server
host.what: The server hostname reachable from the gateway.
host.how: Use the server’s actual network address. SQLite has no server-host field.
host.example: db.example.invalid is illustrative, not a working destination.

port.title: Database port
port.how: Match the selected connector and server. Do not reuse a PLC protocol port.
port.example: PostgreSQL often uses 5432; confirm the actual server.

database.title: Database or SQLite path
database.what: The database name, or the SQLite file path on the gateway host.
database.how: A browser-local path is not a gateway path. Choosing a destination does not prove connectivity or table existence.
database.example: A permitted gateway data path for a new SQLite target.

username.title: Database user
username.what: The database account used by this connector.
username.how: Use the intended least-privileged account. Help never displays saved credentials.

password.title: Database password
password.what: A secret used by the existing database save owner.
password.how: Do not paste passwords into names, notes or examples. A masked stored value is not the original password.
password.example: No credential example or current secret is shown.

schema.title: Default database schema
schema.what: The connector’s schema namespace when this database kind exposes one.
schema.how: Changing a connector schema invalidates destination evidence; it does not move existing rows.
schema.example: public only for a PostgreSQL server configured to use it.

selector.title: Circuit being edited
selector.what: Selects the existing circuit draft owner, not a conversion of another profile.
selector.how: Switching keeps recoverable offline drafts; unresolved or unsaved operations use the existing navigation guard.
selector.example: Return to the same circuit to continue its own draft.

name.title: Circuit name
name.what: The human-readable name associated with the circuit identity.
name.how: Use a meaningful name before confirming a counter; renaming does not fabricate source bindings.

instantaneous.title: Record measurements
instantaneous.what: Includes the selected source in the existing instantaneous profile.
instantaneous.how: The saved reduction and member role remain authoritative; this toggle does not redefine a source.
instantaneous.example: Voltage as a measurement; a status still keeps its status meaning.

cumulative.title: Record counter changes
cumulative.what: Includes selected confirmed counters in the cumulative profile.
cumulative.how: Counter definitions, reset/rollover semantics and first-baseline handling still apply.
cumulative.example: The first baseline has no delta; it is not a zero consumption record.

instantaneousInterval.title: Measurement interval
instantaneousInterval.what: The existing instantaneous profile recording interval.
instantaneousInterval.how: Use the unit shown by this field and its existing interval validator, not the PLC polling cadence.
instantaneousInterval.example: A saved latest profile stays latest; changing the interval does not make it mean.

cumulativeInterval.title: Counter interval
cumulativeInterval.what: The time window used by the existing cumulative profile.
cumulativeInterval.how: Use the displayed unit and current limits; do not infer a fresh baseline from a form change.
cumulativeInterval.example: A confirmed counter reports the difference for its completed interval.

role.title: Member meaning
role.what: Distinguishes measurement, raw counter and state for the existing profile.
role.how: Only appropriate numeric roles are offered. Saved roles cannot be silently rewritten; counter proof remains required.
role.example: State and raw counters keep latest rather than being averaged.

storageMode.title: Storage organization
storageMode.what: The existing table storage mode, separate from result calculation.
storageMode.how: Use only capability-approved options. A saved mode may be locked; partitioning is not an automatic history migration.
storageMode.example: Monthly mode is available only when the selected backend supports it.

recreate.title: Recreate missing managed structure
recreate.what: The existing opt-in policy for missing managed database structure.
recreate.how: Read the inline impact and schema confirmation. This does not grant permission to erase history.
recreate.example: A missing table still requires fresh ownership and schema checks.

semantics.title: Counter behavior
semantics.what: Declares whether this source is a counter or a signed counter.
semantics.how: Choose the actual source semantics: counter disallows negative increments; signed_counter allows them. This saves the source definition, not the recording draft.
semantics.example: Use signed_counter only for a source whose documented cumulative value may decrease.

unit.title: Counter engineering unit
unit.what: The unit explicitly confirmed with the counter definition.
unit.how: Use the source’s real engineering unit. This field does not rescale samples by itself.
unit.example: kWh only when the counter really measures kilowatt-hours.
